overall: The AG found the Boston Public Improvement Commission did not violate the Open Meeting Law: notices were posted properly, the broad minutes audit was declined, and the minutes concern drew only a reminder and encouragement.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Commission failed to post notice of its meetings as required by the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: We also note that that the Commission posts notices of its meetings on the City’s website in compliance with the Open Meeting Law’s meeting notice posting requirement.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Commission failed to create adequate minutes of its meetings; the AG declined a database-wide review without a specific meeting date.
allegations.key_passage: As such, without a particular meeting date to investigate, we will not review the entire database of meeting minutes to determine the Commission’s compliance with the requirement that it maintained sufficient minutes of its meetings.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged some Commission minutes were insufficient; AG shared the concern that some minutes lacked a summary of discussion but found no violation overall.
allegations.key_passage: We encourage the Commission to review its minutes to ensure that they include a summary of the discussions on each subject, as the law requires.

allegations.summary: In a request for further review, complainant alleged minutes were approved by staff rather than the Commission; raised for the first time, so not reviewed.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review allegations raised for the first time in a complaint filed with our office.
